content.overview: Forest conservation in India is governed primarily by the Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980, which restricts the dereservation of forests or use of forest land for non-forest purposes except with prior approval of the Central Government. Constitutional support appears in Article 48A (State duty) and Article 51A(g) (citizen duty). The framework sits alongside the Environment (Protection) Act, wildlife law and NGT jurisdiction for environmental disputes arising from scheduled enactments.
content.glance: Ask: (1) Forest land or dereservation? (2) Non-forest purpose? (3) Central approval under Forest (Conservation) Act? (4) Constitutional duties 48A/51A(g)?
content.study:
The core statutory control is prior Central approval for non-forest use of forest land. Do not invent specific clearance numbers or later amendment labels without the official text.

No new case invented.

sections.heading: Forest (Conservation) Act 1980
sections.body: Restricts dereservation of forests and use of forest land for non-forest purposes without prior approval of the Central Government.

sections.heading: Non-forest purpose
sections.body: Use of forest land for purposes other than forestry — the statutory definition and exceptions must be read from the Act as in force.

sections.heading: Constitutional support
sections.body: Art. 48A directs the State to protect forests; Art. 51A(g) imposes a citizen duty to protect the natural environment including forests.

sections.heading: Coordination
sections.body: Wildlife protection, EPA and EIA may apply concurrently where the project affects forest and other environmental media.

sections.heading: Forum
sections.body: NGT for Schedule I environmental civil questions; High Court under Art. 226 where maintainable.

examples.title: Diversion without approval
examples.body: Project seeks to use forest land for a non-forest industrial purpose without Central approval under the Forest (Conservation) Act — statutory restriction is attracted.

hypotheticals.question: Can a State dereserve forest land for industry on its own?
hypotheticals.analysis: The Forest (Conservation) Act requires prior approval of the Central Government for dereservation or non-forest use of forest land as defined.

distinctions.title: Forest conservation vs wildlife protection
distinctions.left: Forest land use and dereservation control under Forest (Conservation) Act.
distinctions.right: Protection of wild animals, birds and plants under the Wildlife (Protection) Act framework.

misconceptions.trap: Any tree-cutting dispute is automatically under the Forest (Conservation) Act.
misconceptions.correction: The Act targets dereservation and non-forest use of forest land; other tree/forest local laws may apply on different facts.

questionsAndAnswers.answer: Restriction on dereservation/non-forest use; Central approval; constitutional support.
